questions.question: Explain the difference between physical features and human features, with two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Physical features are made by nature, such as mountains, valleys, plains, plateaus, rivers and lakes. Human features are made by people, such as roads, bridges, houses, farms, dams and towns.

questions.question: Describe the shape of South Africa's land, using the words coastal plain, escarpment and plateau.
questions.expected_answer: South Africa is shaped like an upside-down saucer. A narrow, low coastal plain runs along the coast. Behind it, the land rises steeply up the Great Escarpment. On top is the high, fairly flat plateau, which covers most of the interior.

questions.question: Give three ways in which physical features affect where and how people live.
questions.expected_answer: People build towns, roads and farms on flat land because it is easier; towns grow near rivers for water; mountains are hard to cross, so roads use passes and tunnels; the coast gives harbours, fishing and tourism; and high land is cooler.
